rounds.text: Polychem Ltd is trading at a modest price-to-book ratio of 1.34x on a book value of ₹ 1,482 with a share price of ₹ 1,990 [E1], sitting near the bottom of its 52-week range at just 16% of the way up from its low [E4], which presents an attractive entry point. The business generates an exceptional return on capital employed of 56.4% [E5], demonstrating elite capital efficiency that is heavily discounted by the current micro-cap valuation of ₹ 79.6 Cr [E2]. Top-line expansion remains structurally intact over the long term, backed by a 10-year compounded sales growth of 13% [E7] and a 5-year compounded sales growth of 12% [E8], complemented by recent sequential and year-over-year momentum with sales up recently [E53] and rising at 6% over the trailing twelve months [E10] and 13% YoY [E52]. Long-term shareholders have been rewarded with a 10-year compounded share price growth of 17% [E12] and a 5-year compounded share price growth of 26% [E13], proving the compounding capability of the underlying asset over meaningful horizons. Conceded: the return on equity sits at -7.1% [E6], 3-year compounded sales growth contracted by -5% [E9], trailing twelve-month profit growth fell by -231% [E11], and price growth has recently outpaced profit growth by 199% [E46].

Polychem Ltd is severely under-appreciated by the market, trading near the bottom of its 52-week range at just 16% of that range [E4] while offering a clean price-to-book valuation of 1.34x against a book value of ₹ 1,482 [E1]. This disconnect is starkly illogical given the company's elite capital efficiency, highlighted by a phenomenal ROCE of 56.4% [E5]. Furthermore, top-line fundamentals are actively recovering and expanding, demonstrated by a 13% YoY sales growth screen reason [E52], sequential sales growth QoQ [E53], and steady long-term compounding with 10-year sales growth at 13% and 5-year sales growth at 12% [E7, E8]. Long-term shareholders have already been rewarded with consistent compounded share price growth of 17% over 10 years and 26% over 5 years [E12, E13], proving the underlying long-term wealth creation engine remains intact. Conceded: [E6, E11, E57].
